headline: High-risk default interaction: Kestra can write/egress broadly while OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP/REST inputs, creating injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can write files, emit logs/messages, and call HTTP/Slack/email, while OpenBBTerminal uses MCP servers and a connect-once-consume-everywhere pattern. That creates a plausible bridge where Kestra-produced content is ingested by OpenBB as trusted input. No direct shared channel is documented, so I choose medium rather than low because the interaction is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF Kestra outputs are forwarded into an OpenBB MCP or REST input without sanitization
IF OpenBB parses Kestra-generated text as instructions or parameters
mitigations: Add a strict content boundary between Kestra outputs and OpenBB inputs
Prefix all cross-agent payloads with a machine-validated schema
Disable automatic ingestion of free-form logs/messages into OpenBB
Review one sample workflow for prompt-like fields before enabling the pair

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and can use MCP/REST APIs. If Kestra passes sensitive workflow data into OpenBB, OpenBB can expose it through its API surface; the shared data path is plausible even though no shared workspace is explicitly documented.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows route logs, artifacts, or database data into OpenBB requests
IF OpenBB MCP/REST calls include sensitive financial or licensed data
mitigations: Restrict Kestra-to-OpenBB payloads to non-sensitive fields
Turn off forwarding of logs and artifacts into OpenBB
Use separate credentials for each agent
Add a redaction step before any API call
Audit one end-to-end run for unintended data propagation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad egress; OpenBBTerminal can use MCP servers and REST APIs but cannot write files or spawn subprocesses. The main conflict is shared mutable resource access through APIs or local orchestration, not direct filesystem contention. Because both can act on overlapping external resources and no locking is documented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents target the same external API, dataset, or localhost service
IF orchestration does not serialize their writes or requests
mitigations: Assign disjoint resource scopes to each agent
Serialize access with a simple lock or queue
Separate credentials and API keys
Disable concurrent writes to shared endpoints
Run a one-step dry run to confirm no overlapping mutations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow outputs, logs, and notifications that OpenBBTerminal may consume via MCP/REST. OpenBB’s connect-once-consume-everywhere pattern makes it easy for unverified upstream content to become downstream actions or analyses. Because the pair can turn one agent’s output into the other’s authoritative input, the blast radius can extend to incorrect financial decisions or automated actions.
conditions: IF OpenBB uses Kestra-produced outputs as authoritative market or portfolio inputs
IF downstream OpenBB actions are triggered without independent verification
mitigations: Insert a verification step between Kestra and OpenBB
Require human approval for any downstream action
Pass only structured, typed outputs
Log provenance for every cross-agent field
Disable automatic action execution from OpenBB until tested

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra touches database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. The pair therefore can combine regulated or sensitive classes with different handling expectations, especially if Kestra routes operational data into OpenBB workflows. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so medium fits the plausible policy gap rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated financial data from OpenBB is mixed with Kestra logs, messages, or artifacts
IF retention or access controls differ between the two agents
mitigations: Classify shared fields before enabling the pair
Keep regulated data out of Kestra notifications and logs
Apply the stricter retention policy to both agents
Review secret-handling paths in OpenBB
Document a data-flow map for one representative workflow
